label: upubhub class (textbook, lesson plans, assessments)
summary: A short course a teacher teaches from on upubhub.com: a textbook with discussion topics, one lesson plan per lesson and class assessment settings. The text is written new or converted from the teacher's own files. After the teacher's final sign-off the dashboard can push it to upubhub as private drafts and an invite-only class.
planner_text:
Plan a course package in the project folder, not software. Settings: content source {{content_source}}, class code subject {{subject_code}}, level {{level}} (written as two digits), {{lessons}} lessons, sources: {{sources}}, illustrations: {{illustrations}}, assessments: {{attempts}} attempts, {{strictness}} grading, weighted toward {{emphasis}}. Follow upubhub-class-format.md exactly; the dashboard's course-package check enforces it.
Content source write: agents write original lesson text. Content source provided: the teacher's own files are the text. inputs/textbook.md holds the textbook (a "# " heading per lesson when there is more than one lesson, a "## " heading per section) and inputs/lesson-plans/*.md holds one lesson plan per lesson, in lesson order by file name. Agents copy that text: they never rewrite, shorten, extend or summarise it, and every problem in it goes back to the teacher.
Stories, in order: (1) human sign-off on the course brief: subject, scope, audience, reading level, lesson count and measurable objectives per lesson. (2) human sign-off on the source plan: for write, original writing or named open-licence sources (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0 or public domain) with author and https link; for provided, the teacher confirms they wrote or hold the rights to every provided file and lists any borrowed passage or image the same way. Never invent a licence or a credit; only the teacher can attest to reuse rights. (3) provided only: a read-only agent story titled "Check the provided files": the lesson count is {{lessons}}, every lesson has sections and a lesson plan, no section is empty, each lesson is within 60,000 characters, and images exist with alt text; it writes docs/project/provided-check.md, and each problem becomes a human fix story for the teacher, never an agent rewrite. (4) agent outline: write course/course.json with the class code in `code` (SUBJ:LL-Class name, exactly as the project settings give it), lessons, section headings and objectives, ai_provenance is hand_crafted for provided (the teacher's own words; topics, assessments and structure the pipeline adds do not change that), ai_generated or ai_assisted for write; for provided, lesson titles and section headings are copied from inputs/textbook.md. (5) agent textbook stories, one per lesson and parallel, each producing course/textbook/<lesson>.md with one "## " heading per section exactly as in course.json: written new for write; for provided, the lesson's text copied unchanged apart from heading levels and image paths. (6) agent discussion topics: course/topics.json, at most 12 per lesson, anchors copied from the lesson text. (7) illustrations only when the illustrations setting is yes, using the media stages (inventory, generate in Media studio after spend approval, publish, integrate); images live in assets/img and are referenced from the lesson Markdown with alt text. (8) a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer; for write its findings become fix stories, for provided they become a list for the teacher, who alone changes the text. (9) agent lesson plans, one per lesson, parallel: written new for write; for provided, inputs/lesson-plans files copied unchanged into course/lesson-plans/<lesson>.md. (10) agent assessment settings, one per lesson. (11) agent static verification titled "Verify course package files" with verification_stage "static": re-read every file against the format guide and fix mismatches (for provided, only structure, never the teacher's wording); the dashboard runs the course-package check when the operator accepts this story and lists every problem. (12) agent UPLOAD.md: the step-by-step manual upload and class-setup checklist, kept as the fallback. (13) human final sign-off titled "Approve the course for upubhub": the teacher reads every lesson, lesson plan and assessment and approves the package; nothing leaves this computer before it. (14) human, after the final sign-off: send the course to upubhub with the dashboard's Push to upubhub button (private drafts and an invite-only class), or upload it by hand from UPLOAD.md; then review the drafts, publish lessons, share the textbook, assign lessons and finish the class in upubhub. No containers, deployment, CI, pull requests or application code. No model chooses classroom ids, holds the upubhub token or uploads anything.
failure_points: A lesson heading that differs from course.json by one character breaks the package; copy the headings, do not retype them.
A topic anchor must occur exactly once in its section, on a plain prose line; upubhub rejects anchors inside links, images, code or markup.
upubhub assesses at most 12 topics and 60,000 characters per assigned lesson set; split long lessons instead of trimming quality.
Written text (content source write) is declared ai_generated or ai_assisted, never hand_crafted.
A borrowed passage or image without a credit, an allowed licence and an https source cannot be uploaded; prefer original writing.
The writer checking its own facts misses its own errors; the fact-check story uses a different model and reads the lesson text, not the outline.
Provided text is the teacher's: a conversion that rewords, trims or "improves" it is wrong even when the result reads better. Copy, then report problems.
A provided textbook whose lesson count, headings or lesson plans do not line up with the settings is sent back to the teacher before any outline is written.
Provided text is declared hand_crafted: it is the teacher's own words, and the topics, assessments and lesson structure the pipeline adds do not change that.
visual_checks: The teacher reads every lesson and lesson plan before upload; illustrations are approved in Media studio before they are integrated.
human_signoffs: Approve the course brief and objectives
Approve the source and licence plan
Approve media spending and select/publish illustrations in the project Media tab, when illustrations are requested
Read every lesson, lesson plan and assessment and approve the course for upubhub
Push the course to upubhub (or upload it by hand), then publish and set up the class in upubhub

checks.message: Start with a human sign-off on the course brief and measurable objectives.
Add a human sign-off on the source and licence plan; only the teacher can attest to reuse rights.
Add the static verification story "Verify course package files"; the dashboard runs the course-package check when it is accepted.
Add a read-only fact-check story on a different model from the writer.
Lessons, topics and plans are planned before the outline that fixes their headings.
Uploading, publishing and class setup in upubhub are the teacher's steps.
A course package needs no containers, deployment, CI or pull requests.
End with the teacher's final sign-off "Approve the course for upubhub"; nothing is pushed or uploaded before it.
The final sign-off comes after the course package is verified.
The push to upubhub comes after the teacher's final sign-off.
Pushing to upubhub is the teacher's step, run by the dashboard after the final sign-off; agents never hold the token.
Provided text needs the read-only story "Check the provided files" before the outline.

customize.label: Content source
customize.prompt: write: agents write new lesson text. provided: you put your own inputs/textbook.md (one "## " heading per section, a "# " heading per lesson when there are several) and inputs/lesson-plans/*.md in the project folder, and agents convert them without rewriting.

customize.label: Subject code
customize.prompt: The class code's subject: 3 to 5 capital letters from the list. GEN is the catch-all for everyday general-knowledge topics; NEWS, TECH and ENGR cover how today's things work. Meanings are in class-codes.md.

customize.label: Level
customize.prompt: Reading level as a grade equivalent: 0 kindergarten, 1 to 12 grades, 13 to 16 college years. For a general adult audience, 9 or 10 reads easily. Shown as two digits in the class code.

customize.label: Class name
customize.prompt: The class's name as students will see it, for example Forces and Motion.

customize.label: Subject and scope
customize.prompt: What the course teaches, and what is in and out of scope. Mention vocabulary to avoid or require.

customize.label: Sources
customize.prompt: Where lesson text and images may come from. List each open-licence source (title, author, licence, https link) in the source sign-off.

customize.label: Illustration style
customize.prompt: Style and roughly how many images, if lessons are illustrated.
